Earlier reviews have covered the first of these questions at the level of strain physics, modality differences, clinical practice and sources of discrepancy~\cite{amzulescu2019,smiseth2025}, and more recent reviews cover deep learning for wall-motion analysis across modalities and strain from CMR and computed tomography~\cite{monfared2026review,hussein2026review}. The present review takes a narrower purpose within that literature. It asks how faithfully routine cine CMR can recover \emph{regional or focal} myocardial dysfunction, and how the choice of validation target changes the claim that can be made. Answering that question requires comparing estimator families by their inputs, assumptions, estimands, populations and reference standards: how each family uses image information, representation, priors and supervision to infer motion and strain, and which spatial and temporal scales of measurement its validation evidence supports. Within that comparison, the focal case is the most demanding one, and it is used here as a test of the evidence base, without treating every method paper as if it had set out to solve it.

The learning-based literature began by amortising \cref{eq:registration}. The Strain-8 study scanned 20 healthy volunteers twice on the same day using eight protocols: cine, tagging and DENSE at 1.5 and 3~T, plus 2D and 3D echocardiography. The following examples distinguish the acquisition used at inference, the learning target and the endpoint used for evaluation. They include cine pipelines and methods that analyse the material-sensitive comparator itself. DeepTag estimates motion on tagged images without labels, using bidirectional diffeomorphic registration between consecutive frames and a differentiable composition layer to recover the Lagrangian field, validated by landmark tracking on a clinical tagging dataset~\cite{ye2021deeptag}. Networks trained on synthetic 3D tagged images from a biophysical left-ventricular model have since been evaluated for 3D tagging analysis, including an external human landmark comparison and porcine strain comparisons with manual cine annotations~\cite{buoso2025tagging3d}; like DeepTag, they operate on the comparator acquisition and not on cine. DeepStrain provides an end-to-end cine workflow. It centres the ventricle, segments anatomy, estimates end-diastole-to-phase displacement and derives Green--Lagrange radial and circumferential strain, and the original study reported a CMAC landmark end-point error of \(2.9\pm1.5\)~mm together with scan--rescan repeatability in ten healthy volunteers and high agreement for volumetric measures~\cite{morales2021}. A later single-centre comparison in 47 healthy participants and 533 patients found correlations with manual feature-tracking analysis of 0.83--0.85 for global radial and 0.88--0.91 for global circumferential strain~\cite{morales2022comparison}; in that comparison the comparator is another estimator. These results establish workflow and output properties. Independent dense material truth for the cine motion field is a separate matter, and a prescribed-motion evaluation of DeepStrain is discussed in \cref{sec:knownmotion}.

Clinical studies support the relevance of measuring deformation in those settings. Feature-tracking strain has been associated with functional recovery after myocardial infarction, adverse remodelling and cardiovascular outcomes~\cite{buss2015,reindl2021,chadalavada2024}, and DENSE circumferential strain has shown prognostic association after acute infarction~\cite{mangion2019}. These associations motivate evaluating deformation. They leave open how accurately a regional abnormality has been located or quantified, because a prognostic marker can remain useful despite measurement bias, and a technically accurate motion field may still fail to improve a clinical decision. Analytical validity, biological association and clinical utility are linked questions with separate answers~\cite{raunig2015,puntmann2018}.
Other studies have detected regional feature-tracking abnormalities within infarcted tissue or related regional strain to recovery and outcome~\cite{buss2015,he2024}. Such findings strengthen biological and clinical qualification. They also illustrate why motion accuracy and clinical usefulness should both be studied: a regionally smoothed estimate might retain prognostic signal, whereas a physically accurate field may fail to improve a decision if the endpoint or treatment pathway is poorly specified.

The problem is most prominent for radial strain, for which wall-thickening surrogates, tensor components and layer-specific measurements are not interchangeable. It also affects circumferential comparisons whenever one pipeline reports one-dimensional engineering strain and another reports a component of a two-dimensional Green--Lagrange tensor~\cite{wehner2018,cao2018}.
The paired literature is mixed in a scientifically useful way. A larger comparison of 77 patients with cardiomyopathy and ten controls found relatively small circumferential differences but wide radial differences across tagging, DENSE and three feature-tracking products~\cite{cao2018}. Radial strain is repeatedly less consistent than circumferential or longitudinal strain~\cite{cao2018,militaru2021}. Three features of the measurement explain much of this. The ventricular wall spans relatively few voxels radially, trabeculation complicates the endocardial boundary, and a small contour displacement can produce a large relative change in thickness. Products may additionally calculate radial output from different entities. Clinical studies support the relevance of measuring deformation in those settings. Feature-tracking strain has been associated with functional recovery after myocardial infarction, adverse remodelling and cardiovascular outcomes~\cite{buss2015,reindl2021,chadalavada2024}, and DENSE circumferential strain has shown prognostic association after acute infarction~\cite{mangion2019}. Analytical validity, biological association and clinical utility are linked questions with separate answers~\cite{raunig2015,puntmann2018}.
Global or regional strain has been associated with adverse events across disease cohorts~\cite{mangion2019,chadalavada2024}. Such associations establish prognostic value under the model, covariates and follow-up that were studied. Whether changing management on the basis of the measurement improves outcomes is a further question, and answering it requires a decision context, a comparator, a threshold, the consequences of error and preferably an impact evaluation. The distinction matters most for a regional map, where multiple testing, correlated segments and post hoc threshold selection can produce apparently focal findings.

Temporal strategy adds a further assumption to the objective. Reference-to-frame tracking keeps one reference configuration and must therefore estimate large displacements from it; sequential tracking estimates smaller inter-frame steps and accumulates composition error and drift; groupwise methods estimate all phases jointly under whatever temporal constraint they impose~\cite{metz2011,chen2024}. Balanced steady-state free-precession cine CMR samples a time series of image intensities. In a typical short-axis image, the blood--myocardium interfaces are conspicuous, whereas intramyocardial texture can be weak and changes with coil sensitivity, through-plane motion, partial volume, reconstruction and artefact. The image therefore supplies anatomical and intensity cues without a persistent identity label for every tissue element. Every estimator has to add something to those cues. Feature tracking exploits image features or propagated contours; registration exploits an image-similarity relation; biomechanical models constrain admissible deformation; and learning-based methods import associations learned from training data~\cite{pedrizzetti2016,duchateau2020}. These four categories overlap in practice: a neural network may predict registration parameters, a registration method may use a learned similarity measure, and a biomechanical penalty may be embedded in either.

current_claim_context: Scan--rescan studies are essential for longitudinal use, because they show how much a result may change when the underlying subject is assumed stable. The Strain-8 study scanned 20 healthy volunteers twice on the same day using eight protocols: cine, tagging and DENSE at 1.5 and 3~T, plus 2D and 3D echocardiography. Global repeatability ranged from fair to excellent depending on direction, protocol and field strength, while segmental results were more variable~\cite{bell2025strain8}. A repeatable biased method can still be inaccurate, and a method with good global repeatability can have weaker segmental precision. Both absolute error and variance should therefore be reported at the claimed scale.

current_claim_context: Other designs bound the inference differently. In ten healthy volunteers, model-based deep-learning reconstruction reduced the dispersion of global circumferential strain differences from the fully sampled comparator relative to compressed sensing at reduction factors 6 and 8, while circumferential bias and substantial radial underestimation remained and no regional lesion was tested~\cite{tsuneta2025dlr}. In 19 patients with 51 compressed-sensing acquisitions, retrospective temporal interpolation changed peak longitudinal and circumferential strain while ventricular volumes and ejection fraction stayed similar~\cite{grob2025interp}; stable volumes do not guarantee stable strain. DENT was developed from 5840 patients across nine centres and compared interpolated with acquired cine phases, including prospective image-quality comparisons in 49 patients and 12 healthy participants. It reported image-domain interpolation error and reader assessment; myocardial strain and focal-abnormality recovery were outside its evaluation, and even its deformation vectors were not validated as motion estimates~\cite{morales2024dent}. Reconstruction and motion estimation should therefore be evaluated jointly when the claim is regional, and any proposed mechanism (temporal smoothing, sharpening, alias suppression or hallucination) remains a hypothesis until tested against an attribute-appropriate reference.

Left-ventricular ejection fraction compresses a complex three-dimensional deformation into a chamber-level ratio. That compression has real value: ventricular volumes and ejection fraction are reproducible CMR endpoints, widely understood and embedded in clinical reporting standards~\cite{schulzmenger2020,hundley2022}. Feature-tracking software is attractive because it operates on routine cine and fits existing clinical workflows. Initial contours are propagated through the cardiac cycle, after which strain may be calculated from endocardial length, a myocardial mesh or a vendor-specific deformation field; interior motion is to a large degree interpolated from boundary behaviour~\cite{pedrizzetti2016}. Because each of these steps can be implemented differently, the phrase ``feature tracking'' denotes a family of measurements. Commercial implementations have differed in contour placement, transmural treatment, radial-strain calculation, temporal interpolation and user correction. As a consequence, values may fail to be interchangeable across products or software versions even when repeatability within a product is acceptable~\cite{lim2021,militaru2021}.
Feature-tracking and strain tools change over time. Regulatory clearance may cover a broad software application or specified outputs but does not establish material-motion accuracy for every regional analysis. Product webpages document current availability, not historical algorithms. Studies should therefore record software name, exact version, analysis module, contour convention, manual corrections and any export transformation. Reference intervals and serial thresholds should not be transferred across products without a bridging study~\cite{lim2021,militaru2021,cao2018}.

A third group replaces a generic smoothness penalty with a statement about tissue mechanics or about the function space itself. Qin and colleagues learned the prior in place of writing it down: a variational autoencoder trained on biomechanically simulated deformations defines a manifold of plausible fields, and tracking becomes a search over that manifold, validated on three public cine datasets~\cite{qin2023biomech}. It represents the deformation with a neural network fitted per case under an intensity-similarity term plus a hyperelastic regulariser and a Jacobian penalty for near-incompressibility. Strain follows by automatic differentiation, and Fourier feature mappings allow sharp features in the strain field. It was tested on synthetic examples and a cine benchmark of 15 healthy volunteers~\cite{arratia2023warppinn}. current_claim_context:
Clinical studies support the relevance of measuring deformation in those settings. Feature-tracking strain has been associated with functional recovery after myocardial infarction, adverse remodelling and cardiovascular outcomes~\cite{buss2015,reindl2021,chadalavada2024}, and DENSE circumferential strain has shown prognostic association after acute infarction~\cite{mangion2019}. These associations motivate evaluating deformation. They leave open how accurately a regional abnormality has been located or quantified, because a prognostic marker can remain useful despite measurement bias, and a technically accurate motion field may still fail to improve a clinical decision. Analytical validity, biological association and clinical utility are linked questions with separate answers~\cite{raunig2015,puntmann2018}.
Global or regional strain has been associated with adverse events across disease cohorts~\cite{mangion2019,chadalavada2024}. Such associations establish prognostic value under the model, covariates and follow-up that were studied. Whether changing management on the basis of the measurement improves outcomes is a further question, and answering it requires a decision context, a comparator, a threshold, the consequences of error and preferably an impact evaluation. The distinction matters most for a regional map, where multiple testing, correlated segments and post hoc threshold selection can produce apparently focal findings.

Temporal strategy adds a further assumption to the objective. Reference-to-frame tracking keeps one reference configuration and must therefore estimate large displacements from it; sequential tracking estimates smaller inter-frame steps and accumulates composition error and drift; groupwise methods estimate all phases jointly under whatever temporal constraint they impose~\cite{metz2011,chen2024}. None of these strategies guarantees correct intermediate phases, because a periodic deformation can close perfectly at the end of the cycle and still be wrong in between. Cycle closure is therefore a useful constraint and a useful quality-control signal, and no more than that.
Intensity-based deformable registration estimates a dense field by optimising \cref{eq:registration} directly. The free-form deformation model of Rueckert and colleagues, an affine transform plus a B-spline control lattice with a smoothness penalty, is a widely used representation originating in breast MRI~\cite{rueckert1999}. Groupwise variants remove the dependence on an arbitrarily chosen reference frame. Metz and colleagues fitted an \(n\)D\(+t\) B-spline model to the whole dynamic sequence with spatial and temporal smoothness and an optional cyclic constraint, reporting sub-voxel accuracy on synthetic and thoracic CT data~\cite{metz2011}. More recently, Chen and colleagues replaced the groupwise dissimilarity term with a locally low-rank metric and evaluated it on a 20-case simulation, 100 public cine cases and 16 in-house tagging patients. They reported reduced late-diastolic drift and better correlation with tagging for radial strain in several segments than optical flow, pairwise registration, global low-rank groupwise registration and \(n\)D\(+t\) B-splines~\cite{chen2024}. Feature-tracking software is attractive because it operates on routine cine and fits existing clinical workflows. Initial contours are propagated through the cardiac cycle, after which strain may be calculated from endocardial length, a myocardial mesh or a vendor-specific deformation field; interior motion is to a large degree interpolated from boundary behaviour~\cite{pedrizzetti2016}. Because each of these steps can be implemented differently, the phrase ``feature tracking'' denotes a family of measurements. Commercial implementations have differed in contour placement, transmural treatment, radial-strain calculation, temporal interpolation and user correction. As a consequence, values may fail to be interchangeable across products or software versions even when repeatability within a product is acceptable~\cite{lim2021,militaru2021}.
The product dependence seen by Cao and colleagues was examined directly at 3~T by Militaru and colleagues, who compared three feature-tracking products with tagging in 61 participants. Global longitudinal and circumferential agreement was high, regional and radial agreement varied more, and scar discrimination differed by vendor~\cite{militaru2021}. This pattern supports global and some regional use under specified products, and it warns against interchangeability and against extrapolating global performance to radial or highly local outputs; it does not justify a blanket rejection of feature tracking. Timing has been compared less often than magnitude. Other designs bound the inference differently. In ten healthy volunteers, model-based deep-learning reconstruction reduced the dispersion of global circumferential strain differences from the fully sampled comparator relative to compressed sensing at reduction factors 6 and 8, while circumferential bias and substantial radial underestimation remained and no regional lesion was tested~\cite{tsuneta2025dlr}. In 19 patients with 51 compressed-sensing acquisitions, retrospective temporal interpolation changed peak longitudinal and circumferential strain while ventricular volumes and ejection fraction stayed similar~\cite{grob2025interp}; stable volumes do not guarantee stable strain. DENT was developed from 5840 patients across nine centres and compared interpolated with acquired cine phases, including prospective image-quality comparisons in 49 patients and 12 healthy participants. It reported image-domain interpolation error and reader assessment; myocardial strain and focal-abnormality recovery were outside its evaluation, and even its deformation vectors were not validated as motion estimates~\cite{morales2024dent}. Reconstruction and motion estimation should therefore be evaluated jointly when the claim is regional, and any proposed mechanism (temporal smoothing, sharpening, alias suppression or hallucination) remains a hypothesis until tested against an attribute-appropriate reference.
Accelerated reconstruction can alter temporal sharpness, noise texture and edge appearance, all of which may affect downstream motion estimation even when conventional image-quality scores remain acceptable. Primary evidence is encouraging but endpoint-specific. In REGAIN, global feature-tracking strain from 49 participants showed near-zero mean differences between separately acquired accelerated and GRAPPA breath-hold cine, with non-zero limits of agreement~\cite{yoon2023regain}. CineVN's paired 18-volunteer comparison found the smallest strain bias among the tested accelerated reconstructions, but all accelerated protocols retained systematic peak radial/circumferential bias; the 46-patient demonstration had no conventional reference and included segmentation-related slice exclusions~\cite{vornehm2024cinevn}. In ten healthy volunteers, model-based DLR reduced the dispersion of global circumferential strain differences from full sampling at high reduction factors relative to compressed sensing, while bias and radial underestimation remained~\cite{tsuneta2025dlr}. DENT improved image-phase interpolation and reader-rated temporal presentation across a large multicentre development set and prospective testing, but it did not evaluate myocardial strain or validate its deformation vectors as tissue motion~\cite{morales2024dent}. These measured findings motivate joint reconstruction--estimator tests; they neither show nor imply that deep learning erases focal abnormalities.

Multi-view and mesh-based designs target through-plane motion. MulViMotion fuses short-axis and long-axis cine in a hybrid 2D/3D network with a shape-regularisation module providing weak supervision, evaluated on 580 UK Biobank subjects~\cite{meng2022mulvimotion}. DeepMesh represents the heart as a 3D mesh of endocardial and epicardial surfaces, propagates a template mesh into subject space and estimates vertex-wise displacement through a differentiable mesh-to-image rasteriser, so that vertex correspondence is maintained across frames and subjects~\cite{meng2024deepmesh}. CardioMorphNet takes the shape idea further: a recurrent variational autoencoder with separate posteriors for segmentation and motion, trained by recursively registering segmentation maps without an intensity-based similarity loss, validated on UK Biobank and M\&Ms by comparing warped masks with reference masks and yielding voxel-wise uncertainty maps~\cite{movahed2026cardiomorphnet}. Predictive uncertainty and accurate warped masks are valuable outputs, with two limits: the uncertainty is not automatically a calibrated regional error, and a Bayesian output is not automatically an abstention policy. STCMT-Net represents cardiac motion through keypoints extracted without supervision and reconstructs the dense field as a weighted combination of basis vectors from matched keypoint pairs, evaluated on 4D CT and cine MRI with a strain analysis reported to separate patients under different conditions~\cite{qiao2026stcmt}.

Numerical phantoms make exact correspondence available. A simple realistic phantom showed that spatial and temporal resolution can materially affect feature-tracking measurements~\cite{adams2023}. MRXCAT2.0 couples statistical shape, biophysical simulation and tissue texture to produce healthy and pathological cine-like images paired with known functional ground truth~\cite{mrxcat2023}. Other in-silico heart models and DENSE-SIM extend controlled testing of strain pipelines and acquisition effects~\cite{mukherjee2024,barbaroux2025}. The design that such resources make possible, a graded regional deficit measured against a material reference while the estimator is held fixed, has a precedent outside cine: Yeon and colleagues compared tagged circumferential shortening with implanted sonomicrometry crystals in a canine coronary-ligation model, with both methods separating ischaemic from remote myocardium~\cite{yeon2001sonomicrometry}. This provides a precedent for regional reference-based testing, although it is not a controlled sweep of lesion size or severity in routine cine.
MRXCAT2.0 provides a useful prescribed-focal example: an evaluation of DeepStrain by a separate development team. Four left-ventricular cases were generated (normal, dilated, hypertrophic and infarcted; ejection fractions 51\%, 34\%, 41\% and 49\%). An elliptical free-wall scar was prescribed in the infarct case, while remote compensation preserved its ejection fraction. The underlying abnormality differed by component: remote-to-scar peak systolic strain changed from 0.95 to 0.30 radially, from \(-0.18\) to 0.01 circumferentially and from \(-0.18\) to \(-0.17\) longitudinally. Radial strain was markedly reduced but retained a substantial residual value; circumferential strain approached zero, while longitudinal strain changed little. These are prescribed tissue values, not errors of the estimator~\cite{mrxcat2023}.
The generated domain also limits interpretation. The evaluation used one scar geometry and SNR 30, and myocardial texture was removed during image generation. TextNet and DeepStrain both used ACDC data: independence of the evaluating team does not establish independence of the image domain, although shared dataset use alone is not evidence of leakage. The inspected source does not identify the evaluated DeepStrain release or weights. The component-specific errors could reflect image formation, wall thinning and partial volume, training data or estimation constraints; the experiment does not isolate these contributions~\cite{mrxcat2023}.

Balanced steady-state free-precession cine CMR samples a time series of image intensities. In a typical short-axis image, the blood--myocardium interfaces are conspicuous, whereas intramyocardial texture can be weak and changes with coil sensitivity, through-plane motion, partial volume, reconstruction and artefact. The image therefore supplies anatomical and intensity cues without a persistent identity label for every tissue element. Every estimator has to add something to those cues. Feature tracking exploits image features or propagated contours; registration exploits an image-similarity relation; biomechanical models constrain admissible deformation; and learning-based methods import associations learned from training data~\cite{pedrizzetti2016,duchateau2020}. These four categories overlap in practice: a neural network may predict registration parameters, a registration method may use a learned similarity measure, and a biomechanical penalty may be embedded in either.
Feature-tracking software is attractive because it operates on routine cine and fits existing clinical workflows. Initial contours are propagated through the cardiac cycle, after which strain may be calculated from endocardial length, a myocardial mesh or a vendor-specific deformation field; interior motion is to a large degree interpolated from boundary behaviour~\cite{pedrizzetti2016}. Because each of these steps can be implemented differently, the phrase ``feature tracking'' denotes a family of measurements. Commercial implementations have differed in contour placement, transmural treatment, radial-strain calculation, temporal interpolation and user correction. As a consequence, values may fail to be interchangeable across products or software versions even when repeatability within a product is acceptable~\cite{lim2021,militaru2021}.

A third group replaces a generic smoothness penalty with a statement about tissue mechanics or about the function space itself. Qin and colleagues learned the prior in place of writing it down: a variational autoencoder trained on biomechanically simulated deformations defines a manifold of plausible fields, and tracking becomes a search over that manifold, validated on three public cine datasets~\cite{qin2023biomech}. WarpPINN states the physics explicitly. It represents the deformation with a neural network fitted per case under an intensity-similarity term plus a hyperelastic regulariser and a Jacobian penalty for near-incompressibility. Strain follows by automatic differentiation, and Fourier feature mappings allow sharp features in the strain field. It was tested on synthetic examples and a cine benchmark of 15 healthy volunteers~\cite{arratia2023warppinn}. WarpPINN-fibers adds a fibre-stretch penalty and reported improved landmark tracking and strain-curve prediction on a synthetic phantom and the same healthy benchmark~\cite{alvarez2026warppinn}. Liu and colleagues combine the mechanical and temporal arguments in a space--time finite-element correlation framework with region-specific biomechanical regularisation and a data-driven temporal decomposition. Their evaluation is the most layered in this group: one synthetic dataset with ground-truth motion and strain, three public datasets with landmarks or masks and a clinical dataset with masks, against two feature-tracking and four deep-learning baselines~\cite{liu2026fe}. Implicit neural representations of intramyocardial motion and strain have also been presented in the 2026 STACOM proceedings; no abstract accompanies the record retrieved, so that study is not characterised here~\cite{bell2026inr}.

Intensity-based deformable registration estimates a dense field by optimising \cref{eq:registration} directly. The free-form deformation model of Rueckert and colleagues, an affine transform plus a B-spline control lattice with a smoothness penalty, is a widely used representation originating in breast MRI~\cite{rueckert1999}. Groupwise variants remove the dependence on an arbitrarily chosen reference frame. Metz and colleagues fitted an \(n\)D\(+t\) B-spline model to the whole dynamic sequence with spatial and temporal smoothness and an optional cyclic constraint, reporting sub-voxel accuracy on synthetic and thoracic CT data~\cite{metz2011}. More recently, Chen and colleagues replaced the groupwise dissimilarity term with a locally low-rank metric and evaluated it on a 20-case simulation, 100 public cine cases and 16 in-house tagging patients. They reported reduced late-diastolic drift and better correlation with tagging for radial strain in several segments than optical flow, pairwise registration, global low-rank groupwise registration and \(n\)D\(+t\) B-splines~\cite{chen2024}. Optical flow itself offers another route to local correspondence: Wang and colleagues combined intensity and shape-feature invariance in a gradient-based method for cine and tagged MR, evaluated on realistic simulations and preliminary clinical data~\cite{wang2019opticalflow}. Two further designs supply correspondence through geometry or mechanics in place of image similarity: a Laplace-based mapping between successive contours~\cite{elnakib2015laplace} and variational assimilation of cine observations into a contraction model~\cite{tuyisenge2016assimilation}. Each was tested on synthetic data with in-vivo feasibility, and in both the inferred trajectory depends on the modelling assumption. Anatomy-aware, pyramidal and online-adaptive methods change the problem along the same lines, by altering the evidence available to the optimiser and the class of admissible fields~\cite{chen2020anatomy,yu2020mpn,yu2020foal}.

Left-ventricular ejection fraction compresses a complex three-dimensional deformation into a chamber-level ratio. That compression has real value: ventricular volumes and ejection fraction are reproducible CMR endpoints, widely understood and embedded in clinical reporting standards~\cite{schulzmenger2020,hundley2022}. Regional motion and strain are attractive precisely in the clinical settings where such hidden changes matter: focal infarction, heterogeneous cardiomyopathy, dyssynchrony, early dysfunction and treatment response.

Other designs bound the inference differently. In ten healthy volunteers, model-based deep-learning reconstruction reduced the dispersion of global circumferential strain differences from the fully sampled comparator relative to compressed sensing at reduction factors 6 and 8, while circumferential bias and substantial radial underestimation remained and no regional lesion was tested~\cite{tsuneta2025dlr}. In 19 patients with 51 compressed-sensing acquisitions, retrospective temporal interpolation changed peak longitudinal and circumferential strain while ventricular volumes and ejection fraction stayed similar~\cite{grob2025interp}; stable volumes do not guarantee stable strain. DENT was developed from 5840 patients across nine centres and compared interpolated with acquired cine phases, including prospective image-quality comparisons in 49 patients and 12 healthy participants. Reconstruction and motion estimation should therefore be evaluated jointly when the claim is regional, and any proposed mechanism (temporal smoothing, sharpening, alias suppression or hallucination) remains a hypothesis until tested against an attribute-appropriate reference.
Accelerated reconstruction can alter temporal sharpness, noise texture and edge appearance, all of which may affect downstream motion estimation even when conventional image-quality scores remain acceptable. Primary evidence is encouraging but endpoint-specific. In REGAIN, global feature-tracking strain from 49 participants showed near-zero mean differences between separately acquired accelerated and GRAPPA breath-hold cine, with non-zero limits of agreement~\cite{yoon2023regain}. CineVN's paired 18-volunteer comparison found the smallest strain bias among the tested accelerated reconstructions, but all accelerated protocols retained systematic peak radial/circumferential bias; the 46-patient demonstration had no conventional reference and included segmentation-related slice exclusions~\cite{vornehm2024cinevn}. Intensity-based deformable registration estimates a dense field by optimising \cref{eq:registration} directly. The free-form deformation model of Rueckert and colleagues, an affine transform plus a B-spline control lattice with a smoothness penalty, is a widely used representation originating in breast MRI~\cite{rueckert1999}. Groupwise variants remove the dependence on an arbitrarily chosen reference frame. Metz and colleagues fitted an \(n\)D\(+t\) B-spline model to the whole dynamic sequence with spatial and temporal smoothness and an optional cyclic constraint, reporting sub-voxel accuracy on synthetic and thoracic CT data~\cite{metz2011}. More recently, Chen and colleagues replaced the groupwise dissimilarity term with a locally low-rank metric and evaluated it on a 20-case simulation, 100 public cine cases and 16 in-house tagging patients. They reported reduced late-diastolic drift and better correlation with tagging for radial strain in several segments than optical flow, pairwise registration, global low-rank groupwise registration and \(n\)D\(+t\) B-splines~\cite{chen2024}. Optical flow itself offers another route to local correspondence: Wang and colleagues combined intensity and shape-feature invariance in a gradient-based method for cine and tagged MR, evaluated on realistic simulations and preliminary clinical data~\cite{wang2019opticalflow}. Two further designs supply correspondence through geometry or mechanics in place of image similarity: a Laplace-based mapping between successive contours~\cite{elnakib2015laplace} and variational assimilation of cine observations into a contraction model~\cite{tuyisenge2016assimilation}. Each was tested on synthetic data with in-vivo feasibility, and in both the inferred trajectory depends on the modelling assumption. The following examples distinguish the acquisition used at inference, the learning target and the endpoint used for evaluation. They include cine pipelines and methods that analyse the material-sensitive comparator itself. DeepTag estimates motion on tagged images without labels, using bidirectional diffeomorphic registration between consecutive frames and a differentiable composition layer to recover the Lagrangian field, validated by landmark tracking on a clinical tagging dataset~\cite{ye2021deeptag}. DeepStrain provides an end-to-end cine workflow. It centres the ventricle, segments anatomy, estimates end-diastole-to-phase displacement and derives Green--Lagrange radial and circumferential strain, and the original study reported a CMAC landmark end-point error of \(2.9\pm1.5\)~mm together with scan--rescan repeatability in ten healthy volunteers and high agreement for volumetric measures~\cite{morales2021}. A later single-centre comparison in 47 healthy participants and 533 patients found correlations with manual feature-tracking analysis of 0.83--0.85 for global radial and 0.88--0.91 for global circumferential strain~\cite{morales2022comparison}; in that comparison the comparator is another estimator. These results establish workflow and output properties. Independent dense material truth for the cine motion field is a separate matter, and a prescribed-motion evaluation of DeepStrain is discussed in \cref{sec:knownmotion}.

Intensity-based deformable registration estimates a dense field by optimising \cref{eq:registration} directly. The free-form deformation model of Rueckert and colleagues, an affine transform plus a B-spline control lattice with a smoothness penalty, is a widely used representation originating in breast MRI~\cite{rueckert1999}. Groupwise variants remove the dependence on an arbitrarily chosen reference frame. Metz and colleagues fitted an \(n\)D\(+t\) B-spline model to the whole dynamic sequence with spatial and temporal smoothness and an optional cyclic constraint, reporting sub-voxel accuracy on synthetic and thoracic CT data~\cite{metz2011}. More recently, Chen and colleagues replaced the groupwise dissimilarity term with a locally low-rank metric and evaluated it on a 20-case simulation, 100 public cine cases and 16 in-house tagging patients. They reported reduced late-diastolic drift and better correlation with tagging for radial strain in several segments than optical flow, pairwise registration, global low-rank groupwise registration and \(n\)D\(+t\) B-splines~\cite{chen2024}. Optical flow itself offers another route to local correspondence: Wang and colleagues combined intensity and shape-feature invariance in a gradient-based method for cine and tagged MR, evaluated on realistic simulations and preliminary clinical data~\cite{wang2019opticalflow}. Two further designs supply correspondence through geometry or mechanics in place of image similarity: a Laplace-based mapping between successive contours~\cite{elnakib2015laplace} and variational assimilation of cine observations into a contraction model~\cite{tuyisenge2016assimilation}. Each was tested on synthetic data with in-vivo feasibility, and in both the inferred trajectory depends on the modelling assumption. Anatomy-aware, pyramidal and online-adaptive methods change the problem along the same lines, by altering the evidence available to the optimiser and the class of admissible fields~\cite{chen2020anatomy,yu2020mpn,yu2020foal}.
A second group builds cardiac structure into the estimator. Qin and colleagues learned motion estimation and segmentation jointly, sharing a multi-scale encoder between an unsupervised Siamese recurrent spatial-transformer branch and a segmentation branch, in 220 subjects~\cite{qin2018joint}. Zheng and colleagues learned a pixel-wise ``apparent flow'' between two cine phases semi-supervised from a large unsegmented and a small expert-segmented set, then derived per-segment radius and thickness time series whose nine features classified ACDC pathology with 95\% and 94\% accuracy on the training and test sets~\cite{zheng2019apparent}. In that study the motion representation is validated through its usefulness for a downstream label, a pattern that recurs in \cref{sec:supervised}. Motion Pyramid Networks introduced multi-scale fused estimation with a cyclic teacher--student training procedure~\cite{yu2020mpn}, and FOAL added online adaptation of a learned estimator to a new sequence at test time~\cite{yu2020foal}. A 2025 study uses a memory-based model over all cine frames and evaluates supervision choices in 271 patients. Its abstract reports EPEs of 1.02~mm for the base model, 0.95~mm with end-diastolic distance-map supervision and 0.91~mm with full supervision, compared with 1.19~mm for a retrained RAFT baseline. Its evaluation points were manually initialised on the first-frame contours and propagated by conventional feature tracking; they were not motion-training targets. The reported EPE therefore measures agreement with those tracked points. Global peak-strain correlations provide a separate endpoint~\cite{portal2025semisup}.

Known-motion resources allow investigators to test representation capacity, recovery at a chosen signal-to-noise ratio and sensitivity to sampling or regularisation. Existing work has varied resolution~\cite{adams2023}, varied analysis regularisation~\cite{barbaroux2025}, or represented regional pathology in simulated motion~\cite{mrxcat2023,zhou2018straus}. These are useful precedents for the proposed validation programme. The surviving search records do not establish whether all combinations of graded lesion size, severity, transmurality and fixed-estimator evaluation have already been studied. Here, graded attribute recovery is proposed as a research priority, rather than justified by a claim of field-wide absence. Simulation results remain conditional on the anatomy, mechanics, image formation and pathology represented; paired in-vivo comparisons are needed to assess transfer.
STRAUS contains 18 \emph{virtual patients}. These arise from three volunteer-derived multimodal templates, each driven through one healthy and five pathological electromechanical states (left bundle branch block, left-anterior-descending, left-circumflex and two right-coronary-artery ischaemia patterns), so the 18 cases share three anatomies. Each virtual case provides 3D cine MR, three tagged-MR orientations, ultrasound and framewise meshes; the paper used engineering strain for its regional curves~\cite{zhou2018straus,strausdata}. The meshes therefore support known-correspondence displacement and strain calculations when coordinate system, reference frame, mesh identity and temporal sampling are matched. What they cannot supply is the full distribution of human anatomy, disease, image artefact or model error.
